title: Cost Threads: lightweight per-token attribution panel & CSV export prototype
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Design a compact, composable Cost Threads panel for the Redwood Console that surfaces token-level cost attribution inline with routes and model rollouts, and supports a lightweight CSV export for downstream chargeback. The panel should be embeddable in the Route Details page and Dashboard cards; prioritize fast scanability for engineers and finance analysts.

Background: Current cost UIs are heavyweight (full ledgers or heatmaps) and require multiple clicks to reach per-token attribution. Customers want a concise view to: (1) identify expensive prompts quickly, (2) see attribution by model variant and user segment, and (3) export a compact CSV for chargeback and analytics.

User problems addressed: 
- Developers need to reason about per-request unit economics without leaving the Console.
- Finance/Platform teams need an exportable, predictable schema for hourly billing adjustments and audits.
- Product managers need to compare cost delta across rollouts (A/B, canary) with minimal cognitive load.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) UI mockups for desktop and tablet that fit a 320–760px panel width.
2) Prototype interactive in Figma with two modes: Summary (sparkline + top-3 token contributors) and Deep dive (expanded attribution table).
3) CSV export that matches the lightweight schema in attachments and supports sampling controls (full, 1-in-N).
4) Performance constraints documented: panel render must not add >150ms to route details load in hosted Console UIs.
5) Usability test with 6 engineers/2 finance users and prioritized feedback list.

Success metrics: 
- 40% reduction in time-to-identify-high-cost-requests during first-run tasks.
- Export adoption: 20% of teams with billing workflows use the CSV within 6 weeks of launch.

Notes on scope/trade-offs: 
- We deliberately avoid a full token-labeled transcript in this phase to keep rendering costs low; plan for a follow-up that surfaces token positions on demand.
- Attribution attribution model: primary attribution will be by message chunk + model variant; request-level metadata (route, user segment) will be required for export.

decisions: Keep the first iteration token-agnostic in-line and only surface token contributors as aggregated 'top token fragments' to reduce rendering overhead.

CSV schema will be columnar with normalized keys: timestamp, route_id, request_id, model_variant, token_fragment, token_count, token_cost_usd, attribution_weight, user_segment. Sampling mode will append a 'sample_rate' column.

Render mode: default 'Summary' (compact row + sparkline); user can expand to 'Deep dive' which requests a precomputed attribution payload from metrics API. This avoids per-token on-demand tokenization in the browser.

Performance SLO: panel must return a precomputed payload within 120ms for 95th percentile in hosted Console; otherwise, show 'sampled' notice and a link to full export. Engineering to add a metrics flag (ENG-21542).
